Y000001.name: Bartlett Yancey
Y000001.bio: Bartlett Yancey was a Democratic-Republican U.S. Representative for North Carolina's 9th congressional district (1813–1817). Yancey worked as a lawyer.

Y000002.name: Joel Yancey
Y000002.bio: Joel Yancey was a Jacksonian U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 10th congressional district (1827–1831).

Y000003.name: William L. Yancey
Y000003.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000003.bio: William L. Yancey was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Alabama's 3rd congressional district (1844–1846). Yancey worked as a lawyer and journalist.

Y000004.name: Teodoro R. Yangco
Y000004.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000004.bio: Teodoro R. Yangco was a Resident Commissioner from the Philippine Islands (1917–1920).

Y000005.name: George L. Yaple
Y000005.photoCredit: Evening News Association (Detroit, MI), publisher., Public domain
Y000005.bio: George L. Yaple was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Michigan's 4th congressional district (1883–1885). Yaple worked as a lawyer and judge.

Y000006.name: Ralph Yarborough
Y000006.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000006.bio: Ralph Yarborough was a Democratic U.S. Senator from Texas (1957–1971). Yarborough worked as a lawyer and judge, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of World War II.

Y000007.name: Robert M. Yardley
Y000007.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000007.bio: Robert M. Yardley was a Republican U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 7th congressional district (1887–1891). Yardley worked as a lawyer.

Y000009.name: John B. Yates
Y000009.bio: John B. Yates was a Democratic-Republican U.S. Representative for New York's 13th congressional district (1815–1817). Yates worked as a lawyer and judge and was a veteran of the War of 1812.

Y000011.name: Richard Yates Jr.
Y000011.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000011.bio: Richard Yates Jr. was a Republican politician from Illinois who served as Governor of Illinois (1901–1905) and U.S. Representative (1919–1933). Yates worked as a lawyer and journalist.

Y000012.name: Richard Yates Sr.
Y000012.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000012.bio: Richard Yates Sr. was a politician from Illinois who served as U.S. Representative (1851–1855), Governor of Illinois (1861–1865) and U.S. Senator (1865–1871), changing party over time (Whig, then Republican). Yates worked as a lawyer.

Y000013.name: Sidney R. Yates
Y000013.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000013.bio: Sidney R. Yates was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Illinois's 9th congressional district (1949–1963, 1965–1999). Yates worked as a lawyer and diplomat, served in the U.S. Navy and was a veteran of World War II.

Y000014.name: Gus Yatron
Y000014.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000014.bio: Gus Yatron was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 6th congressional district (1969–1993). Yatron worked as an athlete.

Y000015.name: George H. Yeaman
Y000015.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000015.bio: George H. Yeaman was a Unionist U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 2nd congressional district (1862–1865). Yeaman worked as a lawyer and judge.

Y000016.name: Jesse Johnson Yeates
Y000016.bio: Jesse Johnson Yeates was a Democratic U.S. Representative for North Carolina's 1st congressional district (1875–1879, 1881). Yeates worked as a lawyer and was a veteran of the Civil War.

Y000017.name: Archibald Yell
Y000017.bio: Archibald Yell was a politician from Arkansas who served as U.S. Representative (1836–1839, 1845–1846) and Governor of Arkansas (1840–1844), changing party over time (Jacksonian, then Democrat). Yell worked as a lawyer and judge, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of the War of 1812 and the Mexican–American War.

Y000018.name: C. H. Yoakum
Y000018.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000018.bio: C. H. Yoakum was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Texas's 3rd congressional district (1895–1897). Yoakum worked as a lawyer.

Y000019.name: Seth H. Yocum
Y000019.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000019.bio: Seth H. Yocum was a National Greenbacker U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 20th congressional district (1879–1881). Yocum worked as a lawyer, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of the Civil War.

Y000020.name: Samuel S. Yoder
Y000020.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000020.bio: Samuel S. Yoder was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Ohio's 4th congressional district (1887–1891). Yoder worked as a lawyer and judge, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of the Civil War.

Y000021.name: Tom Yon
Y000021.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000021.bio: Tom Yon was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Florida's 3rd congressional district (1927–1933).

Y000022.name: Tyre York
Y000022.bio: Tyre York was an Independent Democratic U.S. Representative for North Carolina's 7th congressional district (1883–1885). York worked as a physician.

Y000023.name: Thomas Jones Yorke
Y000023.bio: Thomas Jones Yorke was a Whig at-large U.S. Representative from New Jersey (1837–1839, 1841–1843). Yorke worked as a judge.

Y000024.name: Sam Yorty
Y000024.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000024.bio: Sam Yorty was a Democratic U.S. Representative from California (1951–1955). Yorty worked as a lawyer and was a veteran of World War II.

Y000025.name: Jacob Yost
Y000025.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000025.bio: Jacob Yost was a Republican U.S. Representative for Virginia's 10th congressional district (1887–1889, 1897–1899).

Y000026.name: Jacob Senewell Yost
Y000026.bio: Jacob Senewell Yost was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 5th congressional district (1843–1847).

Y000027.name: Henry M. Youmans
Y000027.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000027.bio: Henry M. Youmans was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Michigan's 8th congressional district (1891–1893). Youmans worked as a businessperson.

Y000028.name: Andrew Young
Y000028.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000028.bio: Andrew Young was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Georgia's 5th congressional district (1973–1977). Young also served as U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations (1977–1979). Young worked as a clergy member and diplomat.

Y000029.name: Augustus Young
Y000029.bio: Augustus Young was a Whig U.S. Representative for Vermont's 4th congressional district (1841–1843). Young worked as a lawyer and judge.

Y000030.name: Bryan Young
Y000030.bio: Bryan Young was a Whig U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 5th congressional district (1845–1847).

Y000031.name: C. W. Bill Young
Y000031.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000031.bio: C. W. Bill Young was a Republican U.S. Representative from Florida (1971–2013). Young worked as a businessperson and served in the U.S. Army. Young died in office in 2013.

Y000032.name: Clarence Clifton Young
Y000032.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000032.bio: Clarence Clifton Young was a Republican at-large U.S. Representative from Nevada (1953–1957). Young worked as a lawyer and judge, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of World War II.

Y000033.name: Don Young
Y000033.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000033.bio: Don Young was a Republican at-large U.S. Representative from Alaska (1973–1997, 1997–2003, 2003–2022). Young worked as an educator and served in the U.S. Army. Young died in office in 2022.

Y000034.name: Ebenezer Young
Y000034.bio: Ebenezer Young was an at-large U.S. Representative from Connecticut (1829–1835). Young worked as a lawyer and businessperson.

Y000035.name: Edward Lunn Young
Y000035.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000035.bio: Edward Lunn Young was a Republican U.S. Representative for South Carolina's 6th congressional district (1973–1975). Young was a veteran of World War II.

Y000036.name: George M. Young
Y000036.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000036.bio: George M. Young was a Republican U.S. Representative for North Dakota's 2nd congressional district (1913–1924). Young worked as a lawyer and judge.

Y000037.name: H. Casey Young
Y000037.bio: H. Casey Young was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Tennessee's 10th congressional district (1875–1881, 1883–1885). Young worked as a lawyer.

Y000038.name: H. Olin Young
Y000038.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000038.bio: H. Olin Young was a Republican U.S. Representative for Michigan's 12th congressional district (1903–1913). Young worked as a lawyer.

Y000039.name: Isaac D. Young
Y000039.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000039.bio: Isaac D. Young was a Republican U.S. Representative for Kansas's 6th congressional district (1911–1913). Young worked as a lawyer.

Y000040.name: James Young
Y000040.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000040.bio: James Young was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Texas's 3rd congressional district (1911–1921). Young worked as a lawyer.

Y000041.name: James R. Young
Y000041.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000041.bio: James R. Young was a Republican U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 4th congressional district (1897–1903). Young worked as a journalist, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of the Civil War.

Y000042.name: John Young
Y000042.bio: John Young was a Whig politician from New York who served as U.S. Representative (1836–1837, 1841–1843) and Governor of New York (1847–1848). Young worked as a lawyer.

Y000043.name: John Andrew Young
Y000043.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000043.bio: John Andrew Young was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Texas's 14th congressional district (1957–1979). Young worked as a lawyer and judge and served in the U.S. Navy.

Y000044.name: John Duncan Young
Y000044.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000044.bio: John Duncan Young was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 10th congressional district (1873–1875). Young worked as a lawyer and judge.

Y000045.name: J. Smith Young
Y000045.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000045.bio: J. Smith Young was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Louisiana's 5th congressional district (1878–1879). Young worked as a lawyer and judge.

Y000046.name: Lafayette Young
Y000046.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000046.bio: Lafayette Young was a Republican U.S. Senator from Iowa (1910–1911).

Y000047.name: Milton Young
Y000047.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000047.bio: Milton Young was a Republican U.S. Senator from North Dakota (1945–1981). Young also served as President pro tempore of the Senate.

Y000048.name: Pierce M. B. Young
Y000048.bio: Pierce M. B. Young was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Georgia's 7th congressional district (1868–1869, 1870–1875). Young worked as a diplomat and was a veteran of the Civil War.

Y000049.name: Richard Young
Y000049.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000049.bio: Richard Young was a Republican U.S. Representative for New York's 5th congressional district (1909–1911).

Y000050.name: Richard M. Young
Y000050.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000050.bio: Richard M. Young was a Democratic U.S. Senator from Illinois (1837–1843). Young worked as a lawyer and judge.

Y000051.name: Robert A. Young
Y000051.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000051.bio: Robert A. Young was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Missouri's 2nd congressional district (1977–1987). Young served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of World War II.

Y000052.name: Samuel H. Young
Y000052.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000052.bio: Samuel H. Young was a Republican U.S. Representative for Illinois's 10th congressional district (1973–1975). Young worked as a lawyer and educator, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of World War II.

Y000053.name: Stephen M. Young
Y000053.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000053.bio: Stephen M. Young was a Democratic politician from Ohio who served as U.S. Representative (1933–1937, 1941–1943, 1949–1951) and U.S. Senator (1959–1971). Young worked as a lawyer, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of World War I and World War II.

Y000054.name: Thomas L. Young
Y000054.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000054.bio: Thomas L. Young was a Republican politician from Ohio who served as Governor of Ohio (1877–1878) and U.S. Representative (1879–1883). Young worked as a lawyer, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of the Civil War.

Y000055.name: Timothy R. Young
Y000055.bio: Timothy R. Young was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Illinois's 3rd congressional district (1849–1851). Young worked as a lawyer.

Y000056.name: William Albin Young
Y000056.bio: William Albin Young was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Virginia's 2nd congressional district (1897–1898, 1899–1900).

Y000057.name: William S. Young
Y000057.bio: William S. Young was an Adams U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 11th congressional district (1825–1827). Young worked as a lawyer.

Y000058.name: Harold F. Youngblood
Y000058.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000058.bio: Harold F. Youngblood was a Republican U.S. Representative for Michigan's 14th congressional district (1947–1949).

Y000059.name: Oscar Youngdahl
Y000059.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000059.bio: Oscar Youngdahl was a Republican U.S. Representative for Minnesota's 5th congressional district (1939–1943). Youngdahl worked as a lawyer, served in the U.S. Navy and was a veteran of World War I.

Y000060.name: J. Arthur Younger
Y000060.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000060.bio: J. Arthur Younger was a Republican U.S. Representative from California (1953–1967). Younger died in office in 1967.

Y000061.name: David Levy Yulee
Y000061.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000061.bio: David Levy Yulee was a Democratic politician from Florida who served as territorial Delegate (1841–1845) and U.S. Senator (1845–1851, 1855–1861). Yulee worked as a lawyer and businessperson.

Y000062.name: John A. Yarmuth
Y000062.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000062.bio: John A. Yarmuth was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 3rd congressional district (2007–2023). Yarmuth worked as a journalist.

Y000063.name: Kevin Yoder
Y000063.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000063.bio: Kevin Yoder was a Republican U.S. Representative for Kansas's 3rd congressional district (2011–2019). Yoder worked as a lawyer.

Y000064.name: Todd Young
Y000064.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000064.bio: Todd Young is a Republican politician from Indiana who has served as U.S. Representative (2011–2017) and U.S. Senator (since 2017). Young worked as a lawyer and served in the U.S. Navy and Marine Corps.

Y000065.name: Ted S. Yoho
Y000065.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000065.bio: Ted S. Yoho was a Republican U.S. Representative for Florida's 3rd congressional district (2013–2021).

Y000066.name: David Young
Y000066.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000066.bio: David Young was a Republican U.S. Representative for Iowa's 3rd congressional district (2015–2019). Young worked as a businessperson.

Y000067.name: Rudy Yakym III
Y000067.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
Y000067.bio: Rudy Yakym III is a Republican U.S. Representative for Indiana's 2nd congressional district, in office since 2022.
